meta.title: Geardown — the electronic pilot logbook
meta.description: Electronic logbook with exports in EASA, FAA and CASA format: fast entry, automatic night time, licences, FTL and roster. For airline, business and private pilots.

hero.eyebrow: From gear up to gear down · EASA · FAA · CASA
hero.title: Your complete, accurate, up-to-date logbook on your phone, without retyping anything.
hero.subtitle: Log a flight in seconds and Geardown works out the rest: night time, FTL limits, licences and medical. Your CV follows your logbook and job offers are ranked against your experience.
hero.note: %TRIAL%-day trial with no card · No commitment · Your logbook is yours
hero.betaNote: iPhone app in beta (TestFlight), included in the free trial. Android: not available yet.

features.title: Everything a logbook should do
features.subtitle: Ten tools, one source of truth for your flying experience.

logbook.title: Logbook and exports in authority formats
logbook.text: Your flights month by month with their totals, filtered by year, type or operator. Type the registration: Geardown finds the airports and times from the aircraft's ADS-B signals. PDF export in EASA, FAA and CASA formats, plus CSV and Excel.
points: Every AMC1 FCL.050 column, night time from civil twilight
SE / ME / multi-pilot derived from the aircraft
Carry forward your paper logbook totals

import.title: Import any logbook
import.text: CSV or Excel files, exports from other logbook apps, airline PDF statements, your roster, an end-of-flight e-mail pasted as is, or photos of your paper pages. Nothing is saved until you have checked your totals.
points: Automatic column detection, fix before import
“Check your totals” screen before saving
Any import can be undone without touching the rest

audit.title: Automatic audit
audit.text: Geardown reads your logbook like an examiner: overlaps, inconsistent times, duplicates, night time above total, broken continuity. Every warning explains why it shows and what is normal.
points: 17 consistency checks
“Explain” button and a direct link to the flight
Before every check ride or interview

licenses.title: Licences, medical, ratings
licenses.text: Licences, medical certificate, SEP, MEP, TR, IR, FI, LPE… Alerts 90, 30 and 7 days before every expiry, by notification and e-mail.
points: FCL.060 recent experience computed
Scans of your documents in private storage
Custom alert thresholds

ftl.title: Rest and FTL limits
ftl.text: An indicative calculation under EASA ORO.FTL or EU-OPS Subpart Q (business aviation), from your flights and your roster. An aid: it does not replace your operator's FTL monitoring.
points: Max FDP from reporting time, split duty if your operator applies it
7, 14, 28-day and 12-month totals
Minimum rest and weekly rest

stats.title: Experience and statistics
stats.text: Your hours by type, by function, at night and IFR, year by year, and every route on the world map. Your home screen is made of widgets you choose: goals, recent experience, reports.
points: Exact great circle across 19,000 aerodromes
7 / 30 / 90-day / 12-month periods
Goals computed from your logbook and FCL.060

signature.title: Digital flight signature
signature.text: Have a flight signed by your instructor or captain on the screen, or send them a signing link. The entry is locked and its fingerprint sealed.
points: SHA-256 fingerprint: any change after signing is detected
Sign in person or remotely by link
Shown in the PDF export

offline.title: Offline and in sync
offline.text: Geardown works without a network, in flight or on a layover. Your data syncs as soon as you're back online, between the web and your phone.
points: Local database on each device
Hosted in Europe (London)
Automatic backup to your account

jobs.title: Pilot jobs
jobs.text: Openings posted by airlines and operators on their own careers pages. For each one, Geardown checks the ad's criteria against your logbook: met, not met or to verify, with the quote from the ad. Coverage is first of all Europe and business aviation.
points: “My types only” filter, region, licence and right to work
Required hours, type rating and salary read from the posting
Match % computed on your device: your logbook is never sent

cv.title: Pilot CV and application file
cv.text: A CV built from your logbook, with your hours by category (total, PIC, multi-pilot, turbine, night, IFR, per type), tailored to a specific job ad, with a layout designed for the screening software airlines use.
points: Hours by category and by type, always up to date
Pre-send check for applicant tracking systems (ATS), with no guaranteed outcome
PDF, text and JSON Resume export, in English or French

items.a: Your data is stored on your device first, then synced to servers located in London (United Kingdom). Traffic is encrypted (TLS), attachments are kept in a private space and each account can only access its own data. We never sell or share your data.

items.q: Are Geardown exports in EASA format?
items.a: The logbook holds the information FCL.050 requires, in the AMC1 FCL.050 layout. Night time follows the EASA definition (civil twilight). You can print or show the PDF export at any time. The pilot remains responsible for the accuracy of their logbook, and Geardown does not claim the export is accepted or validated by an authority or an airline.
Yes, anytime: PDF in EASA, FAA or CASA format, CSV and Excel. You can also download all your data as JSON from the settings.

items.q: How do I cancel my subscription?
items.a: In one click from the settings (web) or from your store settings (iOS, Android). Your logbook stays readable and exportable after cancellation.

items.q: Can I bring my paper logbook?
items.a: Yes. Enter your paper logbook totals under “Carry forward”: they are added to your totals and shown as “Total from previous pages” in the export. You can also scan your pages or import a file.
Yes. Logging and browsing work offline. Sync resumes automatically once you're back online.

audit.title: Logbook audit
audit.subtitle: Automatic consistency check of your {count} entries.
audit.clean: No issue found. Your logbook is consistent.

codes.timesOrder: Times out of order (off-block, takeoff, landing, on-block)
codes.functionMismatch: Function time (PIC, co-pilot, dual…) inconsistent with total
codes.pilotTimeMismatch: SP SE + SP ME + multi-pilot ≠ total time
codes.landingsWithoutPF: Landings logged while not pilot flying

why.missingTimes: Without block times, total, night and FTL limits cannot be worked out. Add at least off-block and on-block.
why.timesOrder: The order is off-block, take-off, landing, on-block. Usually a wrong date or time zone.
why.overlap: Two flights cannot overlap. Check the times, or a flight entered twice.
why.duplicate: Same date, route, time and registration as another flight: delete one if it is a double import.
why.continuity: Just a reminder: positioning or a flight not logged often explains it. Nothing to fix if that is normal.
why.nightExceedsTotal: Night time is part of total time: it cannot exceed it.
why.ifrExceedsTotal: IFR time is part of total time: it cannot exceed it.
why.functionMismatch: PIC, PICUS, co-pilot and dual share the flight time and cannot exceed it. Instructor or examiner time is logged on top (it may cover the whole flight); a flight with no function counts nowhere.
why.pilotTimeMismatch: Single-pilot SE + single-pilot ME + multi-pilot should equal total time. Empty columns are common after an import; fill them if your format needs them.
why.noLandings: Pilot flying without a landing: FCL.060 recency will not count it.
why.landingsWithoutPF: Usually only the pilot flying logs the landing. Worth a check, nothing serious.
why.futureDate: A flight dated in the future skews totals and limits. Check the year.
why.longBlock: Over 20 h block: possible on a very long flight, otherwise a date or time error.
why.implausibleSpeed: Distance between the airports over flight time gives an unrealistic speed. Often a wrong airport or a flight time too short.
why.unknownAirport: Code not in the aerodrome database: night time and map not worked out for this flight. Check the ICAO code.
why.missingAircraft: Without a registration, hours by type and the export stay incomplete.
why.missingPicName: The EASA format asks for the PIC's name when you are not the PIC.

ftl.title: Flight time limitations (FTL)
ftl.subtitle: Indicative calculation under EASA ORO.FTL for an acclimatised crew member, from your flights and roster.
ftl.disclaimer: A helper: it does not replace your operator's FTL system. The logbook has no report or release times: they are estimated from the settings opposite. A long wait on the ground is never treated as split duty by default: it shows as a "possible split", and the extension counts only if your operator applies split duty and you confirm it (or the roster says so). Not covered: augmented crew, unknown acclimatisation, standby.

yourData.title: Your data is yours
yourData.lead: What Geardown keeps, where, who sees it, and how to take it back or erase it.

items.h: Your logbook lives on your device first
items.p: The logbook is saved on your phone and in your browser and works offline. With an account it syncs between your devices through our servers.
CSV, Excel, PDF in EASA, FAA or CASA format, and all your data as JSON from Settings › My data. Without a subscription, the logbook stays readable and exportable.
From the website or app settings, you delete your account and your data. Deletion is final.
Job offers are ranked on your device: your logbook is not sent for it.
No data is sold or used for advertising. No advertising cookies, no third-party analytics.

items.h: What you don't fill in doesn't exist
items.p: For the medical, Geardown keeps only the class and dates. Optional fields (photo, CV, documents) are stored only if you add them.

thirdParties: Payment: Stripe (web), Apple (App Store); they process your payment, Geardown never sees your card.
Actual flight times (ADS-B): the registration and date are sent to the open ADS-B network adsb.lol, without your name.
Maps: map tiles are loaded from Google Maps or a tile provider, which sees the area shown.
Email: a sending service delivers sign-in codes and the alerts you turned on.
